findings.title: All success criteria trace to tasks with no gaps
findings.description: Every functional requirement has a home: owner/heartbeat at start (Tasks 11, 13, 14), owner-from-creating-write + kill-before-first-heartbeat (Tasks 11, 14, 42 walkthrough step 6), active_step/active_item + finalize clear (Tasks 11, 12), kill -9 → orphaned + wait exit 8 (Tasks 10, 19, 20), v4 UNOWNED keeps waiting (Tasks 8, 10, 19, 20), stale + WARNING + not in default prune (Tasks 10, 19, 20, 33), foreground stall interrupt + dispatch stalled + next-dispatch-succeeds (Tasks 15–18), prune preview/--yes/live-never/unowned/paused protections (Tasks 33–39), no per-run warnings + summary line + -v (Tasks 21, 25, 26), TTY fit + piped no-truncate (Tasks 23–26), pipelines list aligned + params -v (Tasks 27, 28), pipelines show (Tasks 29–31), and the <1 s listing NFR (Task 22a). Technical requirements (liveness row coverage, init_run owner test, RunHeartbeat test, show CLI tests, observer call-order tests, sdk_session fakes, dispatch mapping test, plan_prune/apply_prune tests, fit_widths tests, wait ORPHANED/STALE tests, 199 I/O-bounds 20-running-runs extension, hermetic fixtures, ruff/pyright) all map to their test tasks. Integration requirements (existing 932/199 tests pass, 199 hidden-running tests updated) are addressed in Tasks 17, 22, 26. The traceability table in the Context Summary (D1–D13 → tasks) matches the actual task content.

findings.title: Load test and CI gating are handled, not left implicit
findings.description: The slice restates the listing-time NFR (`sq runs list --all` under 1 s, a few hundred files). Task 22a adds `tests/load/test_run_listing_scale.py` with a `MAX_LISTING_S = 1.0` wall-clock assertion and a row-count assertion, satisfying both the success criterion and `.claude/rules/python.md`'s load-test tier (which requires latency/resource-bound assertions, not just functional correctness). CI gating is addressed explicitly in the task: the existing `testpaths = ["tests"]` in `pyproject.toml:82` collects `tests/load/`, and the CI `test` job runs `uv run pytest` with no marker deselection, so a load-test failure fails CI. The existing load tests (`test_usage_reader_loop.py`, `test_grep_timeout.py`, etc.) are gated the same way, so no new CI wiring task is needed; Task 22a states this rather than leaving it implicit.

findings.title: Task 32 has no commit marker; its work folds into Task 35's commit
findings.description: Task 32 (StateManager.scan_runs + report-file pattern, with its own inline tests) is a tested, working point but carries no `**Commit**:` marker. Its changes are bundled into Task 35's commit (`feat: add plan_prune selection and protection`). This is acceptable per the commit-marker guidance (markers are not required after every task, and a file with none is acceptable), and the bundle is still a coherent, tested point. No action required; noted for completeness.

findings.title: Sequencing respects dependencies with no circular ordering
findings.description: The parts follow the design's Development Approach order: spike (Task 2) → no-behavior-change RunObserver refactor (Part A, Tasks 4–7) → schema v5 + liveness core (Part B, Tasks 8–14) → foreground stall (Part C, Tasks 15–18) → wait/listing (Part D, Tasks 19–22a) → renderer (Part E, Tasks 23–28) → show/prune (Part F, Tasks 29–39) → docs/issues/verification (Part G, Tasks 40–42). Dependencies are honored: ActiveItem is defined in Task 4 before run_liveness (Task 9) and the recorder progress writes (Task 11) consume it; the liveness core (Task 9) precedes its consumers in wait (Task 19), listing (Task 21), and prune (Task 33); the columns renderer (Task 23) precedes the runs/pipelines view moves (Tasks 25, 27) and the prune preview (Task 38, which references "columns renderer, UI spec"); resolve_pipeline (Task 29) precedes show (Task 30). Test tasks consistently follow their implementation tasks (test-with pattern). Commit markers sit at tested points throughout.
